title: Sharpening transfers saturated towers and functorial desingularization rules
statement:
Let $M$ be a fine torsion-free monoscheme with finite affine cover [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization]. Assume additionally that its sharpening $M^\sharp$ is torsion free in the sense of [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]: every sharp stalk has torsion-free group completion. Image under $\lambda:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M/\mathcal M^\times$ bijects coherent ideals on $M$ with coherent ideals on $M^\sharp$. Sharpening identifies corresponding saturated blowups, and hence finite ordered saturated blowup towers, preserving nonempty centers, unit-ideal stages, smoothness of the final object, and recursive pullback along smooth maps between such monoschemes. It preserves the contraction convention of [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup], which retains a nonidentity initial saturation even when its ideal is the whole sheaf.

Sharpening induces a natural bijection between smooth-functorial saturated desingularization rules on the full category of these monoschemes (fine, with finite affine cover, and with both ordinary and sharp stalk group completions torsion free) and such rules on all fine torsion-free fans with finite affine covers. Both rules are functorial by contracted pullback with their ideal centers and order. The bijection preserves identity and composition compatibility. It is defined locally even for fans with no global monoscheme lift: lift affine fans to the monoschemes of their sharp monoids and glue the uncontracted restrictions of the rule on the finite disjoint union of these lifts. The resulting fan tower is finite and independent of the affine cover.

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 3.1.25, 3.1.26, Theorem 3.1.27, Remark 3.1.28, printed p.102; synchronization refers to Remark 2.3.5(ii), p.92. No Stacks tag states this monoidal-geometric result.

proof.text: An ideal of an integral monoid is stable under translation by every unit and its negative. Thus $\lambda^{-1}\lambda(I)=I$ and $\lambda\lambda^{-1}(J)=J$. The same formulas on germs define inverse operations on ideal subsheaves. A finite generating set maps to a generating set, and finitely many local representatives of generators generate the inverse image. Hence coherence, nonemptiness and the whole ideal are preserved. For any sheaf map the ideal generated by images commutes with these operations, since changing a representative by a unit does not change the generated ideal.

Work on an affine monoscheme chart with monoid $P$ and sharp quotient $B$. By [lem-trf-fine-monoid-unit-splitting] choose $P=B\oplus U$, $U\simeq\mathbf Z^s$, over $B$. The ideal corresponding to $J\subset B$ is $J\oplus U$. For a generator $a\in J$, its unsharpened blowup chart is $B[J-a]\oplus U$, because translating a lift of a generator by a unit adds only a unit to its differences. Its saturation is $(B[J-a])^{\rm sat}\oplus U$: a positive multiple lies in the product exactly when its first coordinate lies in $B[J-a]$. The sharpened spectrum is consequently exactly the fan chart for $J$. These charts are fine by [lem-trf-fine-monoid-finite-saturation], and their sharp stalk group completions are torsion free by [lem-trf-fs-face-sharpening]. In particular subsequent levels stay in the stated categories.

On the overlap of the $a$- and $b$-charts the comparison of Step 2 localizes at $b-a$ and $a-b$. Both maps are the identity on the displayed fractions modulo units, so they agree on every triple overlap. The gluing prescription in [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup] gives a canonical global comparison. Starting with an ordered fan tower on $M^\sharp$, pull back its first ideal by Step 1, apply this comparison, and repeat at the next level. Induction on the finite length gives its unique corresponding ordered monoscheme tower. Conversely sharpening this construction recovers every stage and every center. This also proves compatibility with recursive pullback, since Step 1 commutes with generated image ideals and the chart comparison is unchanged by substituting their images.

source.place: VIII 3.1.25(ii)--(iii), p.102, with overlap and induction details.

proof.text: Smooth monoscheme maps sharpen to smooth fan maps: at each stalk $P\to P\oplus\mathbf N^r\oplus\mathbf Z^t$ becomes $\overline P\to\overline P\oplus\mathbf N^r$. For objects, a smooth sharp stalk is $\mathbf N^r$; unit splitting identifies the corresponding unsharp stalk with $\mathbf N^r\oplus\mathbf Z^s$, which is smooth. The converse follows by taking its sharp quotient. For a whole-ideal stage, the saturated blowup is saturation itself; Step 2 shows that it is an isomorphism exactly when its sharp counterpart is. Thus corresponding towers have the same contracted indices, including on a nonsaturated initial object. No reflection of smoothness for arbitrary morphisms is used.

source.place: VIII 3.1.15, 3.1.21--3.1.26, pp.100--102; only the valid direction of the morphism assertion is used.

proof.text: Here is the synchronization argument for any monoscheme rule $R$ in the statement. Along a smooth surjective map no stage is lost: localness of stalk maps reflects a whole pulled-back ideal; and, at a whole-ideal stage, a local smooth product $P\oplus\mathbf N^r\oplus\mathbf Z^s$ is saturated exactly when $P$ is. This product description persists after recursive blowups, since adjoining differences for the center affects only $P$, and saturation acts on that factor. Thus a removable stage after this surjective pullback was already removable before pullback. Functoriality for the identity implies $R(X)=R(X)^c$, so its assigned tower has no such stages. Therefore a smooth surjection gives equality of full ordered towers before contraction.

source.place: VIII 3.1.13--3.1.16, 3.1.22--3.1.26; analogue of 2.3.5(i), p.92. Product verification includes the initial nonsaturated level.

proof.text: For two smooth maps $f,g:Y\to X$, adjoin the identity component and use $f\amalg1,g\amalg1:Y\amalg X\to X$. They are smooth surjections, so Step 5 identifies both full pullbacks with the single tower $R(Y\amalg X)$. Restricting to the $Y$ component proves $f^*R(X)=g^*R(X)$ as uncontracted towers with centers and indices. This argument uses neither a global lift of a fan nor a choice of separate affine resolutions.

source.place: VIII Remark 2.3.5(iii), p.92, applied to the tower definition of 3.1.26.

proof.text: Given a fan rule $Q$, define a monoscheme rule $L(Q)(M)$ by lifting the tower $Q(M^\sharp)$ through Step 3. Its last object is smooth by Step 4. For a smooth map of monoschemes, sharpen it, apply the given functoriality of $Q$, and lift the resulting centers one after another. Steps 1--4 identify the result with the contracted pullback. Since each ideal lift and each chart comparison is prescribed, identity and composite comparisons lift to the same comparisons. This constructs one direction on exactly the corrected monoscheme category.

Conversely let $R$ be a monoscheme rule. For a finite affine cover $F=\bigcup_i S(P_i)$ take the sharp affine models $L_i=\operatorname{Spec}_{\rm mon}P_i$ and $L=\coprod_i L_i$. Here $P_i$ and all its localized sharp stalks have torsion-free group completions by the hypothesis on $F$, so every $L_i$ belongs to our domain. Take the ONE finite tower $R(L)$, and restrict it to each component without contraction. Sharpen these restricted towers. Empty stages on a component are retained at their original indices. We now compare their centers on overlaps before attempting to glue them.

Fix a point in the overlap of two cover charts. For a finite monoid generating set, sum the generators outside the point's prime ideal; its basic open is exactly the generalizations of that point. This is the smallest open neighborhood, affine in each chart, and its sharp sections are the sharp localized stalk monoid $B$ [lem-trf-affine-fan-localization-sections]. Unit splitting writes the two unsharp localizations as $B\oplus\mathbf Z^{s_i}$ and $B\oplus\mathbf Z^{s_j}$ over this same $B$. The common monoscheme $V=\operatorname{Spec}_{\rm mon}(B\oplus\mathbf Z^{s_i+s_j})$ maps smoothly and surjectively onto each. Composing with the two inclusions into $L$ gives two smooth maps $V\to L$. By Step 6 their full pullbacks of $R(L)$ coincide. By Steps 1--3 their sharpenings are precisely the two restricted fan towers on this neighborhood, with all original indices. They therefore have the same ideals at each stage. Such neighborhoods cover the overlap; their comparisons are the identity on the common ideals and fraction charts, so satisfy the cocycle condition.

source.place: VIII 3.1.4(iii), 3.1.11, 3.1.25--3.1.27, pp.98,100,102; expands the local-lift comparison.

proof.text: Glue the first-stage ideals just shown equal: a section belongs to the glued ideal exactly when its restriction belongs to every local ideal. These ideals are coherent because that condition is local and each chart ideal is finitely generated. Glue their saturated blowup charts by the fraction identifications in [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]; Step 9 identifies the restrictions of the next stage. Repeat for the common finite number $n$ of stages of $R(L)$. This constructs a finite tower on $F$, and its terminal sharp stalks are smooth by Step 4 applied to the terminal restrictions of $R(L)$. Each center is nonempty locally. A removable whole-ideal isomorphism globally would pull back to a removable stage on all components of $L$, contradicting identity functoriality for $R(L)$. Thus the glued tower is already contracted globally.

source.place: VIII 3.1.26--3.1.27, p.102; explicit gluing in 2.3.5(ii), p.92.

proof.text: For two covers, use their combined finite cover and the rule on the disjoint union of all its lifts. Restriction to either subunion, followed by contraction, is its assigned rule there. The overlap equality in Step 9 shows that a stage of the combined tower is a whole-ideal isomorphism on one subcover exactly when it is so on the other: each subcover covers all of $F$, so this is a stalkwise test on $F$. Deleting precisely those common indices therefore gives the same glued tower from each cover. The same argument compares two choices of affine lifts, using the common product lifts of Step 9. Denote the resulting cover-independent tower by $S(R)(F)$.

source.place: VIII 3.1.26--3.1.27, p.102; 2.3.5(ii)--(iii), p.92, refinement and index check.

proof.text: For a smooth fan map $g:G\to F$, work on the smallest affine neighborhoods of a point and its image. Their sharp monoids are the corresponding stalks, and [lem-trf-affine-fan-hom-universal] identifies the restricted map with the homomorphism on those stalks. It has form $B\to B\oplus\mathbf N^r$. This is a smooth map of the sharp monoscheme models: after localization, a local map has the form $B'\to B'\oplus\mathbf N^{r-t}\oplus\mathbf Z^t$, because localizing a free orthant inverts exactly a set of coordinates. Apply the smooth functoriality of $R$ to these models. To synchronize all local comparisons, include the finitely many source and target charts in one disjoint union, as in Steps 8--11; the uncontracted comparisons of Step 6 then put every local center at its inherited index. Steps 1--3 identify the sharpened centers with the recursive pullback along $g$. A stage disappears globally exactly when its pulled-back ideal is the whole sheaf and its morphism is an isomorphism, a local test. Thus $S(R)(G)=(g^*S(R)(F))^c$.

source.place: VIII 3.1.13--3.1.16 and 3.1.26--3.1.27, pp.100,102; local smooth maps and synchronized pullbacks.

proof.text: The comparisons in Step 12 respect identities and composition. Before contraction, generated image ideals satisfy $(gh)^*I=h^*(g^*I)$; the maps on every fraction chart make exactly these substitutions. After contraction, the remaining indices are the ordered subsequence of stages that survive these same local tests. Removing an earlier whole-ideal isomorphism cannot change a later ideal or its pullback. Iterating contraction therefore gives the same indices and fraction maps as contracting once. The gluing comparisons are identities on the same local centers, so also obey these equalities globally.

Finally $S(L(Q))=Q$: on the disjoint union of the sharp affine models, lifting and sharpening recover $Q$ by Step 3, and its smooth-surjective cover pullback retains every global index by the argument of Step 5; gluing hence recovers $Q(F)$. In the other direction cover $M$ by affine monoschemes and apply unit splitting to each. Each is a smooth surjective lift of the sharp model. On disjoint unions these maps are still smooth surjections. Functoriality and Step 5 therefore identify $R$ on this cover with the lifted towers used to form $L(S(R))(M)$. Their ideals agree on the cover and hence agree globally, at every stage. Step 3 identifies the towers and their ordered centers. Thus $L(S(R))=R$, with the identity and composition compatibilities already checked. This proves the corrected rule bijection without requiring a global lift of $F$.

source.place: VIII 3.1.25--3.1.27, p.102; finite-cover reconstruction of 2.3.5(ii), p.92.
